newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea intervenes to cap won's rise.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea intervenes to cap won's rise.

text.p: The Bank of Korea intervened in Friday's afternoon trading to cap the won's rise, offering to buy dollars at 902.50 won in three-month forward trading, and 928.00 in one-year forward trading, dealers said.
The central bank offered to buy $30 million in each of the forward trades, dealers said.
The tone for the dollar weakened as foreign funds began to flow in as a result of the higher foreign stock limit.
Dealers estimated such fund inflows at some $500 million to $600 million by next week.
The foreign stock ownership ceiling expanded to 23 percent today from 20 percent.
